Simulated lake chemistry with correlated random-walk state

Source: R/lake_chemistry.R
lake_chemistry.Rd

A state-space dataset for five lakes observed monthly across 60 months. The latent process is a correlated random walk across lakes (two regional clusters share positive innovation correlation, a fifth lake is independent). The observation equation adds a binary treatment indicator that switches on at month 31, with heterogeneous slopes across lakes: two lakes respond positively and three respond negatively.

Usage

lake_chemistry

Format

A data.frame with 300 rows and the following fields:

series

factor identifying the lake (alpine, boreal, coastal, delta, estuary); duplicated as lake.

time

integer month index from 1 to 60.

y

numeric chemistry measurement (Gaussian); duplicated as chemistry.

lake

factor, alias of series.

month

integer month index, alias of time.

treated

integer (0/1) treatment indicator; switches on from month 31 onwards in all lakes.

chemistry

numeric chemistry measurement, alias of y.

Details

A pooled fit with one treatment slope for all lakes reports an effect near zero with a wide credible interval. The positive and negative responses cancel. A state-space fit (trend_formula = ~ RW(cor = TRUE)) with a treatment slope for each lake recovers the response of every lake.

True generative components:

  • Per-lake intercepts (centred).

  • Latent random walk with cross-lake innovation correlation 0.6 between (alpine, boreal) and (coastal, delta), independent for estuary. Innovation standard deviation 0.25.

  • Heterogeneous treatment slopes: (alpine = +0.8, boreal = +0.6, coastal = -0.5, delta = -0.7, estuary = -0.6).

  • Observation noise sigma = 0.4.

See also

RW() for the trend, residual_cor() to extract the fitted correlations between lakes, ranef.mvgam() for the lake slopes, mvgam_data() to check the data.

Examples

data(lake_chemistry)
mvgam_data(lake_chemistry, family = gaussian())
#> ✔ Data check passed for family 'gaussian (link = identity)'.
#> • series: 5 levels
#> • time:   1 to 60
#> • n obs:  300 (0 NA)


# \dontrun{
# A model with the structure the data were simulated from
mod <- mvgam(
  formula = y ~ treated + (treated || lake),
  trend_formula = ~ RW(cor = TRUE),
  data = lake_chemistry,
  family = gaussian(),
  chains = 2, silent = 2
)
summary(mod)
#>  Family: gaussian 
#>   Links: mu = identity; sigma = log 
#> Formula: y ~ treated + (treated || lake) 
#>    Data: lake_chemistry (Number of observations: 300) 
#>  Series: 5 
#>  Trends: RW 
#>   Draws: 2 chains, each with iter = 2000; warmup = 1000; thin = 1; 
#>          total post-warmup draws = 2000
#> 
#> == Observation Model ==
#> Multilevel Hyperparameters:
#> ~lake (Number of levels: 5)
#>               Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS

#> sd(treated)       1.09      0.69     0.09     2.83 1.00      421      266
#> 
#> Regression Coefficients:
#>           Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS

#> treated      -0.37      0.64    -1.67     0.87 1.00      753      772
#>

#> sigma_trend[boreal]      0.26      0.06     0.17     0.39 1.00      937
